### the-dock-keeps-a-window-as-large-as-the-display

*hurt 2 · below the seam · K959 · M1564 · M1568 · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** Bare wallpaper has nothing above it: the pointer is over the Desktop when no window on screen lies under it. Levels are small numbers, and the window server's list comes front to back by level.
- **Happened:** A Mac at rest lists the Dock's window over the whole display (0 0 1024 768) at level 20, the menu bar at 24 and its items at 25. Palettes are at 3, open menus at 101. Finder's icons and the wallpaper are full-display windows at levels such as -2147483603. The list is not sorted by level: the Dock's level 20 window is listed among those behind everything. Judged naively nothing is ever bare, or a menu counts as wallpaper. What a Mac in daily use has there (widgets) is not known.

- **Arbor copes:** PointerSurface.under is a list of what is harmless, not of what is not: it allows what a Mac at rest was seen to have, and `whatMayBeWaiting` takes everything else to be waiting for the click.

### appkit-pushes-panels-out-from-under-the-menu-bar

## identity

Identity: what counts as a window, an app or a display, and whether it is the same one as before.

### apps-restore-their-windows-late-and-under-new-numbers

*hurt 1 · at the seam · K020 · K1282 · K438 · K1471 · K1497 · K459 · M1066 · touches `moved-unasked`*

- **Expected:** The windows in the saved state are there when Arbor starts, under their numbers.
- **Happened:** At login Arbor starts long before most apps have their windows. Apps restore them later and under new numbers, and numbers start again after a reboot, so an old number can be another window's. Launch at login lost the arrangement at every login, and the first window an app shows (a welcome window, a splash) took the place kept for another.
- **Found by:** Review of the app's start and end. Launch at login has not been tried across a logout.
- **Stand-ins play it:** yes (`FakeWindowSystem.renumber`)
- **Guard:** `test: windowsRestoredAfterArborStartsReturnToTheirSlots`; `test: closedWhileItsDisplayWasAwayItLeavesNoPinBehindInTheSavedState`
- **Arbor copes:** Sources/ArborKit/Controller/Controller+PendingSlots.swift keeps a docked window's slot for three minutes, to be claimed by app and title; a pin does not wait yet.
- **Read in:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem+Chaos.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### each-native-tab-is-a-window-of-its-own

*hurt 1 · at the seam · K005 · K123 · K1469 · K1920 · M598 · touches `moved-unasked`, `jolt`*

- **Expected:** One window on screen is one window, with one number and one entry in its app's list for as long as it is open. A window that leaves the list has closed, and choosing a window is reported as a focus change.
- **Happened:** To macOS each tab of a native tab group (Finder, Terminal, Xcode) is a window. Only the one in front is listed; the others leave the list without a word and stay alive. So ⌘T in a docked window gave a new number at the same frame: the new tab floated over the slot and the old one became a ghost. Choosing a tab posts nothing but "main window changed".
- **Found by:** The review of the Accessibility layer, then test windows and the real Terminal on a hosted Mac (macOS 26). A tab dragged out, windows merged, and Xcode have never been tried.
- **Stand-ins play it:** yes (`FakeWindowSystem.openTab`, `FakeWindowSystem.selectTab`, `FakeWindowSystem.closeTab`, `FakeWindowSystem.backgroundTabs`, `World.tabGroups`)
- **Guard:** `test: aNewTabTakesOverTheSlotOfTheWindowItCovers`; `test: switchingBackAndForthBetweenTabsKeepsTheSlot`; `test: aTabThatOpensTallerThanTheSlotIsFittedToIt`; `test: aNewWindowInExactlyTheSamePlaceTakesOver`; `test: closingTheTabInFrontLeavesTheSlotToTheNextTab`; `test: aTabMayDifferInHeightByATabBar`; `test: aGuestWithNativeTabsStaysAGuestWhenItsTabChanges`; `test: aNativeTabThatComesToTheFrontOutOfViewInheritsTheSizeToComeBackTo`; `e2e: open a native tab in a docked window` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: the covered tab leaves no ghost` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: choose the first tab again` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: close the tab in front` (on CI's Macs)
- **Arbor copes:** NativeTabs.successor knows a tab by the same corner and width and a height within 40 points, and `windowReplaced` hands over the slot. A tab chosen from code in a group that is not its app's main window is still noticed late.
- **Read in:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `collab/QUESTIONS.md`, `Sources/ArborCore/NativeTabs.swift`, `scripts/mac-shell/compat-extras.sh`, `Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`

### sheets-panels-and-dialogs-are-no-standard-windows

*hurt 2 · below the seam · touches `focus`*

- **Expected:** Every window the window server lists for an app is a window to arrange.
- **Happened:** A sheet is a child of its window and not one of the app's windows. A utility panel is a floating window to Accessibility, an alert a dialog. When one of them takes the keyboard the system says so, and Arbor's layer passes on only that the keyboard left the known windows. On a hosted Mac the test process had more than four windows at the normal and floating levels, and Arbor managed exactly four.
- **Found by:** A script of claims about real windows on a hosted Mac, where all these checks passed, and experiments with a sheet and a dialog of TextEdit.
- **Stand-ins play it:** yes (`World.extras`, `FakeWindowSystem.strangers`, `FakeWindowSystem.userFocusesNothing`, `FakeWindowSystem.openStrayDialog`)
- **Guard:** `test: standardWindowsAreWindows`; `test: everythingElseInViewIsNot`; `e2e: windows that are not standard windows are left alone` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: the panel and the sheet stayed out of it` (on CI's Macs)
- **Arbor copes:** WindowKind.classify takes standard windows only; `StrayDialog` moves a dialog that opens out of view to the middle of the display, once.
- **Read in:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `scripts/mac-shell/proof.sh`, `Sources/arbor-fakemac/World.swift`, `Sources/arbor-fakemac/World+Input.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/AX/AXWindowSystem.swift`

### launch-services-decides-which-bundle-is-arbor

*hurt 4 · machine · K493*

- **Expected:** A bundle is what its path says, one built in a temporary folder can claim the `arbor://` scheme, and starting a copy concerns nobody else.
- **Happened:** Launch Services does not register what lies under /tmp, so a URL can only be tried from where `make install` puts the bundle. `open` makes any copy known under the real bundle id and would hand arbor:// URLs to a bundle that is deleted a minute later. A program started directly from inside a bundle has the bundle's id all the same and registers nothing. An entry for a bundle that is gone stays for a while.
- **Found by:** Mac shell scripts on a hosted Mac: the proof script's URLs, the distribution checks, the bundled watchdog.
- **Stand-ins play it:** partly (`Arbor.bundled`, `World.open`)
- **Guard:** `e2e: the URLs went to the running Arbor, not to a second one` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: a URL runs a command` (on CI's Macs); `tool: lint-mac-shell.py`
- **Arbor copes:** ProcessGuards.claimSingleInstance lets one Arbor run. The bundles that scripts make get identifiers of their own and claim no URL, and the proof script installs its bundle on a throwaway Mac only.
- **Read in:** `scripts/mac-shell/proof.sh`, `scripts/mac-shell/lib-F13.sh`, `scripts/mac-shell/check-F41.sh`, `Sources/arbor-fakemac/World+Arbor.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

## permissions

Permissions: what macOS allows, to whom, and how it says no.

### a-child-has-its-parents-permission

*hurt 1 · below the seam · touches `lost`*

- **Expected:** Arbor either has Accessibility or has not, and an Arbor started again by its watchdog has what it had.
- **Happened:** Started as a child process Arbor answers with the permission of the terminal, or of the hosted Mac's agent. The same binary in a bundle opened through Launch Services answers for itself: it has none, as on a newcomer's Mac. A bundled Arbor started again as a child would be the child of a process that no longer exists; and `open` hands on only the environment variables it is told to.
- **Found by:** Mac shell scripts on a hosted Mac: the first launch in pictures and the bundled watchdog.
- **Stand-ins play it:** **no**
- **Guard:** `e2e: another Arbor took over, with the same home folder and socket` (by hand); `e2e: the watchdog starts Arbor again` (on CI's Macs)
- **Arbor copes:** Watchdog.run starts a bundled Arbor again through `open -n --env`, so that macOS sees the app itself asking.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/App/Watchdog.swift`, `scripts/mac-shell/watchdog-bundle.sh`, `scripts/mac-shell/shots-F10.sh`, `Sources/arbor-e2e/main.swift`, `Sources/arbor-fakemac/World+Arbor.swift`

### a-refusal-comes-from-inside-a-call

*hurt 1 · at the seam · suspected · K848 · M1052 · touches `lost`*

- **Expected:** A call that fails means that the app did not answer.
- **Happened:** With the permission gone every call is taken to answer `apiDisabled`, in the middle of a layout. That is not the app's silence, and the calls to come would be refused as well. Whether calls fail at once on a Mac has never been seen. The stand-in answers a refused `setFrame` with the frame asked for and lists no windows, where today's layer answers nil and goes on giving what it remembers.
- **Found by:** Writing the feature and reading the Accessibility layer. The script that asks a Mac has not run.
- **Stand-ins play it:** partly (`FakeWindowSystem.isDenied`, `FakeWindowSystem.deniedCalls`)
- **Guard:** `test: aRefusedCallIsASecondOpinionTooAndIsActedOnOnceTheCallerHasReturned`; `test: aRefusalThatMacOSDoesNotConfirmChangesNothing`
- **Arbor copes:** WindowSystemEvents.accessibilityWasRefused is sent from inside the call, which answers nil; the controller acts once the caller has returned.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/AX/AXWindowSystem.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/Platform/WindowSystem.swift`, `Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### losing-the-permission-with-a-tap-can-stop-all-input

*hurt 1 · below the seam · suspected · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** Taking the permission away only disables Arbor, and its event taps become harmless.
- **Happened:** macOS has been reported to stop all input when a process loses Accessibility permission while it has an active event tap. This project has not seen it, and the manual check for it is open. In the first run of that check on a hosted Mac (2026-10-15) Arbor had let go of its taps within a second of the loss, and quit and brought its window back afterwards. Whether input stopped meanwhile was not tried: the script's own tools cannot press once the permission is gone from every app.
- **Found by:** Reports from elsewhere, quoted in the spec and in the code.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `test: theTapsWatchdogCountsAsASecondOpinion`; `e2e: Arbor removes its taps within three seconds` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** PointerInput.checkPermission looks once a second while a tap is installed and removes the taps at once.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/Input/PointerInput.swift`, `docs/features/F03-trackpad-gestures.md`, `docs/features/F63-permission-taken-away.md`, `scripts/mac-shell/input-taps.sh`, `docs/TESTING.md`

- **Happened:** An Arbor that is running needs its permission to bring windows back into view when it quits. With the entry cleared first the windows out of view stay there until the new Arbor has its permission.
- **Found by:** Following the install page to the letter and reading what the script prints.
- **Stand-ins play it:** yes (`FakeWindowSystem.isDenied`, `Harness.revokeAccessibility`)

### the-trusted-flag-may-go-on-saying-yes

*hurt 1 · at the seam · M1052 · M1051 · touches `lost`, `input-held`*

- **Expected:** `AXIsProcessTrusted()` says whether Arbor may use Accessibility.
- **Happened:** The flag can go on saying yes after Arbor is removed from the list with the − button, and one no out of the blue may only be the privacy daemon restarting. Seen since, on macOS 26.6.2: under a second after `sudo tccutil reset Accessibility` a running Arbor logged "Accessibility permission is gone (AXIsProcessTrusted says yes, but macOS refused a tap)". The thorough question caught it, and the four taps were gone within one second. How long the flag would have gone on is not known. The stand-in's comment still calls `flagLags` unseen.
- **Found by:** Reading and documentation; then the first run of the session of `input-taps.sh` that takes the permission away, on a hosted Mac on 2026-10-15. Taking it away by hand in System Settings is still on the list of manual checks.
- **Stand-ins play it:** yes (`FakeWindowSystem.flagLags`, `FakeWindowSystem.isDenied`, `FakeWindowSystem.mayUseAccessibility`)
- **Guard:** `test: ifTheFlagLagsTheRefusedCallsTellTheTruthAndTheyAreBelievedThoroughly`; `test: onceTheThoroughWayHasWorkedItsNoIsBelievedAgainstTheFlag`; `test: oneNoFollowedByYesChangesNothingAtAll`; `test: oneNoIsNotBelievedAndIsAskedAboutAgainSoon`; `e2e: Arbor removes its taps within three seconds` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** EventTap.refusal asks the flag and then makes a tap and throws it away; PermissionWatch asks again half a second after a no out of the blue.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/Input/EventTap.swift`, `docs/features/F63-permission-taken-away.md`, `Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `collab/QUESTIONS.md`, `scripts/mac-shell/input-taps.sh`

### without-the-permission-commands-seem-to-succeed

*hurt 1 · at the seam · K002 · K920 · M1052 · touches `lost`, `input-held`*

- **Expected:** A call without the permission fails and somebody notices. The old stand-in's `setFrame` simply worked without it.

### activate-is-only-a-request

*hurt 2 · below the seam · K117 · touches `behind`, `focus`*

- **Expected:** Activating an app brings it forward, whoever asks. A helper tool that activates another process stands in for ⌘Tab.
- **Happened:** Since macOS 14 activation is cooperative: a request from an app in the background may be ignored, and an app comes forward for certain only if the one in front makes way for it. On a hosted Mac (26.6.2) a request from a command-line tool left the old app in front, and the app had to bring itself forward on a signal. The newer `activate()` is not granted to an accessory app in the background either. Asked for from a terminal, Arbor may not be let to the front. A refusal of Arbor's own `focus` has not been seen on macOS 26.
- **Found by:** The third session of the proof script on a hosted Mac, writing the macOS-only code, and the real-window runner's steps that cross from one app to another.

## timing

Timing: how long things take, and what can happen meanwhile.

### an-app-answers-a-move-inside-the-echo-window

*hurt 1 · below the seam · K013 · touches `jolt`, `stuck`*

- **Expected:** What is reported right after Arbor's move is the echo of Arbor's move. Another frame then is a stage of that move, because size, position and size are set one after the other.
- **Happened:** An app can move or resize its window back within 0.05 to 0.1 s of being placed. Within the first 0.15 s the report was swallowed as the echo: the Accessibility layer said no more, Arbor believed the window docked where it was not, and it stayed out of its place for good. At 0.4 s there were two rounds of a fight, then the same silence.
- **Found by:** The review of the Accessibility layer, and traces of a test window that moves itself back, on a hosted Mac (stubborn-fast, stubborn-slow). The real-window runner plays it since. The traces say themselves that the swallowed report lies below what a trace records.
- **Stand-ins play it:** partly (`FakeWindowSystem.stubbornFrames`, `FakeWindowSystem.appsSettle`, `Behaviour.snapsBack`, `FakeWindowSystem.appsReact`)
- **Guard:** `test: anotherFrameInTheFirstMomentIsLookedAtAgain`; `trace: stubborn-fast.expect`; `trace: stubborn-slow.expect`; `e2e: an app that answers every move at once` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: Arbor notices, and gives up on it too` (on CI's Macs)
- **Arbor copes:** EchoFilter.judge calls another frame in the first moment early. The window is looked at again 0.3 s later (`secondLooks`) and reported as moved by its app if it is not where Arbor put it.
- **Read in:** `collab/evidence/traces/README.md`, `Sources/ArborCore/EchoFilter.swift`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `Sources/ArborTestWindows/Commands.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### at-logout-apps-save-their-frames-as-they-quit

*hurt 1 · below the seam · suspected · K022 · M589 · K1794 · touches `lost`, `size-lost`*

- **Expected:** Arbor's own turn to quit is early enough to bring every window back into view, so no app remembers a window in a corner.
- **Happened:** At logout, restart and shutdown every app is asked to quit at about the same time, and apps save their windows' frames as they go. One that saves before Arbor has put windows back restores them in the corner at the next login, and docked windows in the shape of their slots. The workspace's notice that the Mac will power off is said to arrive first, and some app may still cancel the logout. That the notice beats the apps' saving has been read, not run: it needs a real logout.
- **Found by:** A review of the app shell, by reading. No logout has been tried on a Mac.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `test: logoutBringsEveryWindowIntoViewAndACancelledLogoutBringsArborBack`; `test: atLogoutEveryWindowIsAsAQuitWouldLeaveIt`
- **Arbor copes:** Controller.sessionIsEnding lets go of every window as a quit would, in view and in its own size, at the notice. It pauses for two minutes instead of quitting, so that a cancelled logout does not leave the session without Arbor.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/App/ProcessGuards.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/Controller/Controller+Pause.swift`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `collab/QUESTIONS.md`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### a-drag-is-heard-of-a-third-of-a-second-late

*hurt 2 · at the seam · K048 · touches `stuck`*

- **Expected:** The start of a drag is reported before the window moves, then changes and moves of the drag in pairs. The fake's `drag` rests 0.3 s at each point, long enough for a drop target to take.
- **Happened:** Arbor learnt of a drag from an Accessibility notice: 0.28 to 0.34 s after the press, after two or three mouse events, with the pointer 40 to 70 points away and the window already moved. It can come after the pointer has stopped, and then only one more mouse event says where the pointer is: a scripted drag without one showed no preview. With a hold of 0.15 s before a target takes, any drag under about 0.45 s was over too soon, and a docked window was undocked and left floating over the others. Whether the figures still hold now that the window server is asked from the press on is said nowhere.
- **Found by:** The traces drag-to-edge and flick-to-edge and scripted drags on a hosted Mac, and a reviewer playing the feature headless. The pointer tool ends every drag with a rest of 0.15 s and one point aside and back for it.

- **Arbor copes:** WindowGrab.classify decides from the frame at the press, the frame now and the pointer, and the window server is asked at every movement from the press on. A docked window let go before the hold is over goes back to its slot.

### a-dragged-window-may-stand-still-until-the-pointer-is-24-points-away

*hurt 2 · controller · suspected · touches `stuck`*

- **Expected:** "A window follows a drag from the first few points": so a pointer that has gone 24 points with the window standing still is busy with the window's content, and Arbor stops looking (`WindowGrab.patience`). In the stand-ins a window is under the pointer from the first move.
- **Happened:** A window may not have moved at the first drag event, and the pointer can be 24 points away before the window server starts to move it. The press is settled as not about the window, both signs of a drag are ignored until the button comes up, and Arbor misses the whole drag: no preview, nothing docks. Seen plainly for the first time in the first run of `check-displays.sh` on a hosted Mac: of four drags of 1,244 to 1,991 points across two displays, in 30 steps each, three were never taken for drags. The windows moved, and nothing was logged, at any level. In the model it is the distance at the first look that finds the window unmoved that counts, not the time: with the window server 100 ms late a pointer 10 or 24 points away is still followed, one 40 points away is lost, for the whole of the drag. What a person would see there: a floating window let go at the edge is not docked, and a docked one dragged out is put back into its slot a quarter of a second after the release. The board has it as 1.33.
- **Found by:** A suite of real-window checks that is not on the trunk yet, in its first run on hosted Macs, beside its rehearsal on Linux, where this was green; the real Accessibility layer run on Linux against a model of a loaded Mac, which lost such drags and showed how; and `check-displays.sh` in its first run on a hosted Mac on 2026-10-15. That drags are lost was seen. That the 24 points are why is suspected: a trace is to come, and the script's coarse steps may have a share. A unit test of `WindowGrab` holds Arbor to today's rule, so it is no guard: a cure will have to change it.
- **Stand-ins play it:** **no**
- **Guard:** **none**
- **Arbor copes:** **not yet**
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborCore/WindowGrab.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/AX/AXWindowSystem.swift`, `Sources/arbor-fakemac/World+Input.swift`, `scripts/mac-shell/e2e-drag.sh`, `scripts/mac-shell/check-displays.sh`, `collab/BOARD.md`

### a-timeout-belongs-to-one-element

*hurt 2 · below the seam · K958 · touches `slow`, `crash`*

- **Expected:** The messaging timeout set on an app's element holds for its windows' elements, and one set on any element applies to that element. Without one of their own, elements keep the system's default of 6 s.
- **Happened:** A timeout belongs to one element object, and window elements do not go by their app element's. Measured: window elements without a timeout of their own took 1.55 s a call, not 6. Set on the system-wide element it becomes the whole process's and covers every element, those made on the fly included. A timeout of 0 means the default of six seconds, not "do not wait".
- **Found by:** Measured on a Mac while the real-window code was hardened; the spec does not say in which run. A check of double-clicks on a real Mac lists it among its traps.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `e2e: within three seconds` (on CI's Macs)
- **Arbor copes:** AXWindowSystem.messagingTimeout: one second, set on the system-wide element on purpose, on each app element and on each window element when it is first seen.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/AX/AXWindowSystem.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/Input/DesktopProbe.swift`, `docs/features/F17-real-window-hardening.md`, `docs/features/F37-focus-ring.md`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### app-nap-delays-an-accessory-apps-timers

*hurt 2 · at the seam · suspected · K130 · touches `slow`*

- **Expected:** A quarter-second timer fires after a quarter of a second. `ManualScheduler` runs work exactly when it is due.
- **Happened:** An accessory app with no window on screen is a candidate for App Nap, which delays timers by seconds and lowers priority: put-backs, saves and animations would come late.
- **Found by:** Review of the app shell, by reading. No run has shown a late timer.

- **Guard:** **none**
- **Arbor copes:** ProcessGuards.start begins an activity (`userInitiatedAllowingIdleSystemSleep`) that lasts until Arbor stands down.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/App/ProcessGuards.swift`, `Sources/ArborTesting/Fakes.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

Arbor logs nothing in between. Docking where there is room takes 20 to 110 ms on the same Macs. Where the seconds go has not been looked into.

### the-app-learns-of-a-drag-later-than-the-window-server

*hurt 2 · at the seam · K110 · K327 · K329 · M628 · touches `stuck`, `size-lost`*

- **Expected:** While a window is dragged its app reports every move: one "moved" for each mouse event, with the window exactly under the pointer. So the last reported frame is where the window was let go. The fakes send an exact change before every move of the drag.
- **Happened:** The window server moves a dragged window itself and knows its place at once. The app hears about a tenth of a second later and posts eight to ten notices a second, and some apps post none until the drag is over. So the reported frame lags the pointer, also at the release: after a quick drag released at once the last frame reported was 170 points behind. The preview lagged, and a window dropped on the Desktop was remembered short of where it was let go. A read from the window server costs about as much as one from the app (0.18 ms) and cannot hang on the app. Into how many runs of moves one drag is reported differs from one playing to the next, with how often the preview changes on the way.
- **Found by:** Real drags with the real pointer on a hosted Mac, the traces drag-to-edge and flick-to-edge, and the review of the Accessibility layer.
- **Stand-ins play it:** partly (`TraceReplayer`)
- **Guard:** `test: aWindowThatFollowsThePointerIsBeingDragged`; `test: aStaleFrameNeverPutsTheWindowAwayFromThePointer`; `test: everyCommittedTraceReplays`; `test: aPointerThatTravelsWhileTheWindowStandsStillIsNotAboutTheWindow`; `trace: flick-to-edge.expect`; `trace: drag-to-edge.expect`; `trace: textedit-drag.expect`; `trace: terminal-drag.expect`; `e2e: drag it out fast, grabbed near the left end, released without a pause` (by hand); `e2e: a drop preview shows while the button is held` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: the window docks on release` (on CI's Macs)
- **Arbor copes:** AXWindowSystem.lookAtPressedWindow reads the window server's bounds at every move of the pointer, beside the app's notices, and `endGrab` reports those bounds just before the drag ends. Drop targets go by the pointer. Only replays of traces carry the real rhythm: no knob makes a fake app lag or keep silent.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/AX/AXWindowSystem.swift`, `collab/evidence/traces/README.md`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `collab/QUESTIONS.md`, `scripts/mac-shell/shots-F48.sh`

### every-call-is-a-round-trip-to-another-process

*hurt 3 · at the seam · K116 · K184 · K539 · K072 · K1931 · touches `slow`*

- **Expected:** The stand-ins answer at once, so a command costs what Arbor's own code costs.
- **Happened:** Arbor's own work is tens of microseconds; the rest is waiting for other processes. A call takes 0.1 to 0.6 ms from an idle app, 2 to 5 ms for a resize that changes the size, about 9 ms to focus; in traces a `setFrame` took 1 to 20 ms, and 44 ms (Finder) and 101 ms (TextEdit) the first time. A new panel costs about 3 ms when first shown: stepping out to twelve windows took 45 to 53 ms, 30 to 40 of them for a dozen gap panels. A ⇧ mouse-down over a window was held 2.9 ms instead of 0.4 while the window list was read.
- **Found by:** `took` in every trace of real windows; a measuring run of scripts/mac-shell/perf.sh on a Mac with twelve real windows.

- **Arbor copes:** FramePlan makes one call where one does, panels are kept and handed out again, and the stand-ins count calls instead of time. The real window system does not take the hint of `moveTogether` yet.
- **Read in:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `collab/evidence/traces/README.md`, `Sources/ArborTesting/Budget.swift`, `Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

## input

Input: where presses, keys and gestures really go.

### a-click-on-the-wallpaper-also-closes-what-is-open

*hurt 1 · controller · suspected · K1422 · K1423 · K1535 · K857 · K1700 · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** A plain click on the bare Desktop is waited for by nobody but Finder, so asking what is under the pointer is enough to keep it from macOS.
- **Happened:** People click the wallpaper to be rid of an open menu, Spotlight, Control Centre, a Dock stack, a popover or a list of completions. With the guard on, that click would reach nobody and the thing would stay open; an item of Arbor's own menu hanging over the Desktop could not be clicked, Finder would not become active or clear its selection, and an icon would light up when the button comes up, not when it goes down.
- **Found by:** A second reader of the macOS-only code, after the guard had been merged switched on. Nobody has seen the guard at work on a Mac, and the levels of menus, Spotlight and Mission Control have not been measured.
- **Stand-ins play it:** partly (`World.closeMenu`, `World.windowServerList`)
- **Guard:** `test: anOpenMenuAnywhereIsWaitingForTheClick`; `test: arborsOwnMenuIsAMenu`; `test: whateverElseIsUpMayBeWaitingForTheClick`; `e2e: session 3: a click on the Desktop does not sweep the windows away` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** Settings.guardDesktopClicks ships false until the guard has been seen on a Mac; PointerSurface.whatMayBeWaiting gives the click back unless everything above the palettes is what a Mac at rest has there.
- **Read in:** `docs/features/F60-guard-the-wallpaper-click.md`, `Sources/ArborCore/PointerSurface.swift`, `docs/SETTINGS.md`, `Sources/ArborCore/Settings.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### a-silent-tap-freezes-all-input-until-the-next-event

*hurt 1 · below the seam · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** macOS switches a slow tap off by itself, and input goes on.
- **Happened:** With a tap that does not answer the event waits, and so does every event behind it, also of types the tap does not watch. Nothing happens until the next event arrives. If the tap has then been silent for more than about a second (0.6 s was tolerated, 1.8 s was not) macOS switches it off and later events pass.
- **Found by:** scripts/mac-shell/input-taps.sh on a hosted Mac with macOS 26, by stopping Arbor while a witness listens at the far end of the chain of taps.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `test: repeatedSwitchOffsLeaveTheTapsOffForAWhile`; `e2e: session 2: Arbor stops answering, again and again` (by hand); `e2e: after three in a row the mouse-down tap is left off` (by hand); `e2e: it does not wait for Arbor` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** TapHealth leaves all the taps off for thirty seconds after three switch-offs in ten: Arbor gives up its gestures rather than freeze the Mac again.
- **Read in:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `Sources/ArborCore/TapHealth.swift`, `scripts/mac-shell/input-taps.sh`

### a-tapped-event-waits-for-the-callback

*hurt 1 · below the seam · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** An event tap only listens, so it can run on the main run loop like the rest of Arbor.
- **Happened:** macOS holds back every tapped event, for every app, until the tap's callback returns. On the main thread, where one Accessibility call can take a second, every click, drag and pinch on the Mac waited with it. With a healthy tap on a thread of its own a mouse-down takes about 0.2 ms longer to reach its app (0.23 ms without Arbor, 0.41 ms with), and one that needs the window list about 3 ms.
- **Found by:** A review of the input code; then scripts/mac-shell/input-taps.sh on a hosted Mac, where a witness at the far end of the chain of taps measures how late events arrive.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `test: theThreadServesPointerEventsAtInteractivePriority` (on CI's Macs); `test: blocksRunOnTheTapThreadAndReturnTheirResult` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: with Arbor: how long a click on a docked window takes` (by hand); `e2e: none of them was held back` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** EventTapThread runs every tap on a thread of its own: callbacks only decide, taps are paused unless wanted, and logging, commands and drawing hop to the main queue.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/Input/EventTap.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/Input/GestureTap.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/Input/DesktopProbe.swift`, `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`

### an-event-stuck-in-a-tap-is-overtaken-by-later-ones

*hurt 1 · below the seam · K1538 · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** Events leave a tap in the order they came, so a press that was held too long can be given back late (0.4 s was proposed).
- **Happened:** On macOS 26.6 the waiting event stays stuck until the callback answers or the process dies, while the later ones pass. A mouse-down given back late would arrive after its own mouse-up: the stuck press the proposal was meant to prevent.
- **Found by:** scripts/mac-shell/input-taps.sh on a hosted Mac.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** **none**
- **Arbor copes:** Sources/ArborKit/Input/RectangleFramer.swift puts no time limit on a callback: no callback waits (DesktopProbe asks from a queue of its own), and what was held is given back whole and in order.
- **Read in:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `collab/QUESTIONS.md`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### taps-that-share-a-thread-freeze-the-mac-once-each

*hurt 1 · below the seam · suspected · K1205 · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** "Three freezes, then Arbor lets go" can be counted for each tap by itself.
- **Happened:** All taps share one thread, so the event that got past a tap that was switched off waits at the next one. With a count for each tap, two taps on mouse-downs would freeze everybody's input six times before Arbor rested.
- **Found by:** Reading, when a second tap on mouse-downs was written. Nobody has seen the six freezes.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `test: threeFreezesAreTheLimitHoweverManyTapsThereAre`; `e2e: and so is every other tap: they share the thread that was too slow` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** TapHealth is one for the whole tap thread: switch-offs are counted together, and at the third every tap rests.
- **Read in:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`, `Sources/ArborKit/Input/EventTap.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### a-key-is-a-position-not-a-letter

*hurt 2 · at the seam · K082 · K1165 · K1577 · M557 · touches `moved-unasked`*

- **Expected:** ⌃⌥Z is the key labelled Z.
- **Happened:** A key event names a position. On a keyboard that is not a US one shortcuts sat on the US position and the menu showed the US letter: ⌃⌥Z was the key labelled Y in Germany, Q's place is A in France, on Dvorak nothing is where a US keyboard has it. "⌃⌥?" did nothing in Europe, and "/" pressed literally was ⌃⌥⇧7, which overwrote a saved view. Arbor is never the active app and still has to hear of a change of layout.
- **Found by:** Reviews of the input code and of usability. The sample layouts are compared with macOS's own on a Mac; no real key has been pressed.
- **Stand-ins play it:** partly (`SampleKeyLayouts.german`, `SampleKeyLayouts.french`, `SampleKeyLayouts.dvorak`, `SampleKeyLayouts.russian`)
- **Guard:** `test: everyDefaultShortcutWorksOnEveryLayoutAndNoTwoShareAKey`; `test: theSampleLayoutsAreWhatMacOSHas` (on CI's Macs); `test: onAnotherKeyboardLayoutItIsTheKeyThatCounts`; `test: aCharacterMeansTheKeyThatTypesIt`; `scenario: 44-a-german-keyboard.sim`; `e2e: German, selected while Arbor runs in the background` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** Sources/ArborKit/Input/KeyboardLayout.swift reads macOS's tables and listens for a change of input source; KeyLayout says which key types a character.
- **Read in:** `scripts/mac-shell/check-F44.sh`, `Sources/ArborTesting/SampleKeyLayouts.swift`, `Sources/arbor-fakemac/World+Arbor.swift`, `docs/TESTING.md`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### a-rotation-rides-along-with-a-pinch

*hurt 2 · controller · K068*

- **Expected:** A pinch that is swallowed is the whole gesture.
- **Happened:** Two fingers that pinch also turn, and macOS sends the rotation as events of its own. During a pinch Arbor had taken they still reached the app: an ⌥-pinch over a map also turned the map.
- **Found by:** A review of the input code.
- **Stand-ins play it:** **no**
- **Guard:** `test: aRotationThatBeginsDuringArborsPinchIsKeptFromTheApp`; `test: aRotationDuringArborsPinchIsKeptFromTheAppInBothModes`; `e2e: the app gets none of the rotation that began during it` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** GestureRouter keeps a rotation that begins during a pinch of Arbor's from the app, and GestureTap swallows it.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/Input/GestureTap.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

*hurt 2 · below the seam · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** A tap that is made only to see whether macOS allows one, and thrown away at once, does nothing.

### a-wallpaper-click-activates-finder-without-a-window

*hurt 2 · at the seam · touches `moved-unasked`, `focus`*

- **Expected:** An app that comes forward brings its main window, a report says which window has the keyboard now, and the view goes there.
- **Happened:** A click on the wallpaper activates Finder without asking for its last window: its main window is still set, its focused window is not. Reporting the main window would bring a Finder window into view. The keyboard has left every known window and no `windowFocused` says so. The same holds for a sheet, a dialog, a panel and an app that is not observed.
- **Found by:** A review of the app as a person meets it, and comments in the Accessibility layer. The run that showed it is not named.
- **Stand-ins play it:** yes (`FakeWindowSystem.userFocusesNothing`, `World.finderPID`, `World.keyboardLeavesTheWindows`)
- **Guard:** `test: movingTheViewWithNothingFocusedFocusesAWindowInView`; `test: aCommandThatLeavesTheViewWhereItIsLeavesTheFocusAloneToo`; `e2e: a click on the backdrop reaches the Finder's Desktop` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** AXWindowSystem.keyboardLeftTheKnownWindows reports `keyboardFocusMoved`. Only an app's focused window counts, never its main one.
- **Read in:** `collab/QUESTIONS.md`, `Sources/ArborKit/AX/AXWindowSystem.swift`, `Sources/arbor-fakemac/World+Input.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/Platform/WindowSystem.swift`

### an-accessory-app-stays-active-after-its-last-window

*hurt 2 · below the seam · K1756 · K921 · touches `focus`*

- **Expected:** Arbor is never the active app, so "the focused window" is always one of the person's. When a window of Arbor's own closes, the keyboard goes back to the app that had it.
- **Happened:** A window that activates Arbor (the settings, the update window, Help → About Arbor) makes `focusedWindow()` find Arbor's own window. An accessory app that closes its last window stays the active app. So no window has the keyboard until a click or ⌘Tab, the focus ring goes, shortcuts that act on the focused window fail and the rows under Focused Window are grey.
- **Found by:** The real-window runner, at its step "close the settings window", reading the view code, and Mac shell scripts that click a test window again after closing a panel. The About panel's case stands among the manual checks as known and low.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `e2e: give a window the keyboard before opening the settings window` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: the window that had the keyboard has it again` (on CI's Macs); `e2e: close the settings window` (on CI's Macs)
- **Arbor copes:** SettingsWindowController.windowWillClose makes way for the app that was in front when the window opened, and activates it. The update window and About do not do so yet.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/UI/SettingsWindow.swift`, `docs/TESTING.md`, `Sources/arbor-e2e/main.swift`, `Sources/arbor-fakemac/World+Menu.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### clicks-fall-through-what-a-panel-does-not-draw

*hurt 2 · below the seam · K999 · K065 · touches `input-held`*

- **Expected:** A borderless panel gets the clicks inside its frame, where something of it can be seen and nowhere else. The stand-in hands a drag of a gap straight to the controller, so the handles in the gaps were tested and green.
- **Happened:** The window server lets clicks fall through a window's transparent parts unless the window has said that it wants them, and a handle in a gap draws nothing at rest. On real windows the gaps could not be dragged at all until 2026-10-14. The other way round, a panel with alpha 0 still swallows clicks.
- **Found by:** Real input on test windows on a hosted Mac. The panel with alpha 0 comes from notes on the peek's outline, which name no run.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `e2e: drag the gap between two windows` (on CI's Macs)
- **Arbor copes:** SeamPanel says `ignoresMouseEvents = false` out loud, and so do the peek's outline, the minimap and the panel of shortcuts: every panel of Arbor's says one or the other.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/UI/PeekOutlinePanel.swift`, `docs/features/F01-dock-and-zoom.md`, `Sources/ArborKit/UI/AppKitOverlays.swift`, `collab/evidence/gestures-latest.txt`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### launchers-bring-an-app-forward-without-a-click

*hurt 2 · controller · suspected · K1835 · K1308 · M1034 · touches `focus`*

- **Expected:** An app that comes forward within 0.5 s of a click or a modifier key was asked for; any other pushed itself forward.
- **Happened:** Raycast, Spotlight, Alfred, `open <url>` in a terminal, a link clicked in a chat whose browser is slow: no click and no modifier let go in the last half second, so Hold Still turned the app away in silence, every time. A ⌘Tab reported 0.6 s late would be turned away too. The 0.5 s has never been measured on a Mac.
- **Found by:** A working day replayed headless; what launchers do is reasoning, not a recording.
- **Stand-ins play it:** yes (`FakeWindowSystem.comesForward`, `FakeWindowSystem.secondsSinceInput`)
- **Guard:** `test: onlyAFocusChangeRightAfterAClickOrAModifierKeyCountsAsAsked`; `test: whatHoldingStillTurnsAwayIsSaidOnceForEachAppAndHold`; `test: holdingStillAnAppThatComesForwardByItselfStaysOutOfView`; `scenario: 58-hold-the-view.sim`
- **Arbor copes:** Settings.holdStillWhileCameraIsOn ships false, and what Hold Still turns away is said on screen once for each app and hold; counting Return or a launcher as asking is open.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/AX/AXWindowSystem.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### secure-text-entry-keeps-the-keyboard-from-a-panel

*hurt 2 · below the seam · touches `focus`*

- **Expected:** A panel of Arbor's that makes itself key gets the keys. The stand-in for the panels always has them.
- **Happened:** macOS may not let it have the keyboard; secure text entry does that. The keys go to the app behind and cannot be kept from it, and the panel sits there looking as if it had them. What AppKit says is its own book-keeping: whether the window server agreed shows only in where the keys go.
- **Found by:** Read in comments in the source; the run that showed it is not named. The real-window runner only notes what AppKit and Accessibility say.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** **none**
- **Arbor copes:** Sources/ArborKit/UI/FinderPanel.swift has a global monitor, as the name field and the panel of shortcuts have, that closes the panel at a key or a click that went elsewhere.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/UI/CheatSheetPanel.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/UI/NamePanel.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/UI/FinderPanel.swift`, `Sources/arbor-e2e/GoTo.swift`

### taps-see-every-gesture-as-event-type-29

*hurt 2 · below the seam · touches `input-held`, `crash`*

- **Expected:** A tap asks for magnify events by the number NSEvent has for them, and a gesture event says which keys are held.
- **Happened:** Taps see every trackpad gesture as CG event type 29, the number of NSEvent's `.gesture`. NSEvent's `.magnify`, 30, is another event to CoreGraphics (Dock control). Reading `magnification` of any other event raises an exception, and a gesture event may carry no modifier flags.
- **Found by:** Read in comments in the source; scripts/mac-shell/input-taps.sh counts on a hosted Mac what reaches the app.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `e2e: do posted pinches arrive at all? (no Arbor)` (by hand); `e2e: the app gets none of the pinch` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** GestureTap masks `.gesture`, looks at the type before it reads anything else, and asks for the keys held now as well as the event's flags.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/Input/GestureTap.swift`, `scripts/mac-shell/witness.swift`

### arrow-and-function-keys-always-carry-the-fn-bit

*hurt 3 · controller · K126*

- **Expected:** The modifier bits macOS lists for its own shortcuts say which keys are held, so a shortcut with the Globe key can be told from one without.
- **Happened:** On arrow and function keys every listed shortcut carries the fn bit. The tiling of macOS 15 has "Left & Quarters" and its siblings on Globe-⌃⌥⇧ and an arrow, ticked on every Mac, so four of Arbor's shortcuts (⌃⌥⇧ and an arrow) were reported as macOS's as well. They are not.
- **Found by:** A line in the log at the first launch on a tester's Mac with macOS 26.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `test: macOSsTilingOnTheArrowsWithTheGlobeKeyIsNotTakenForArborsShortcuts`; `test: arrowAndFunctionKeysCarryThoseBitsAnyway`; `e2e: K126, for the record: macOS's own shortcuts, raw` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** SystemShortcuts reports a shortcut on such a key only if macOS puts it there by default without the Globe key.
- **Read in:** `collab/QUESTIONS.md`, `Sources/ArborCore/SystemShortcuts.swift`

### with-two-input-sources-arbor-still-gets-control-option-space

*hurt 3 · below the seam · K126 · K081*

- **Expected:** ⌃⌥Space is Arbor's "show everything". Where two input sources are on, macOS's "Select next source in Input menu" sits on the same keys, and it was taken to win.
- **Happened:** Measured on macOS 26.6.2 with a second layout enabled: ⌃⌥Space still reached Arbor and the input source did not change. It is the one measurement there is. A ⌃⌥Space that Arbor does not hold switches the person's keyboard layout, so the harness declines the chord on testers' Macs and scripts use the command instead. In general macOS registers a shortcut that it uses itself without a word, and then one of the two does nothing.

Who gets it?` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** Controller.systemShortcutClashes holds macOS's own shortcuts against Arbor's. `bindings` and `doctor` name the clash and another way to everything, and take no side on who gets the key.

### macos-holds-a-press-until-it-has-brought-the-app-forward

*hurt 4 · machine · touches `input-held`*

- **Happened:** A press on a window of an app that is not in front is passed on only when macOS has brought that app forward: 17 to 137 ms later with no Arbor running, half of them within 77 ms on one Mac. A press on the app in front, or on an icon in the Dock, takes 1 ms. An ordinary day with Arbor was full of the first kind and the runs without Arbor had two of them, so a 99th percentile of 69 ms against 21 was reported as a fault of Arbor's. With the same sixteen presses in every round, the round without Arbor was the slowest of seven.
- **Found by:** A probe in rounds on two hosted Macs, macOS 26.6.2, on 2026-10-15. Its first run had a baseline that was none: after Quit one window covered the others, and every click fell on the app in front already.

### the-first-drag-on-a-mac-left-alone-did-nothing

*hurt 4 · machine*

- **Expected:** The first posted press and drag of the real-pointer test moves the window.
- **Happened:** In the first whole run on a hosted Mac the first drag moved nothing: no preview, no dock, the window still at (270, 140), and all that built on it failed (7 passed, 11 failed). The step began about nineteen minutes into a job on a Mac nobody had touched. In a job of its own, four minutes after the start, the same script has passed 18 of 18 five times. A screen saver was suspected and tried: with one up the first drag went through. It happened again thirteen minutes into a loaded job, again 7 and 11: pointer events arrive, windows move, macOS tiles, and Arbor sees no drag and logs nothing. Suspected: the mouse-down is delivered late, after the first move, by the global monitor on the main thread; or the press is settled as not about the window (a-dragged-window-may-stand-still-until-the-pointer-is-24-points-away).

## looks

Looks: what is on the screen is not what the model said.

### panels-hide-while-their-app-is-in-the-background

*hurt 2 · below the seam*

- **Expected:** A panel that was ordered to the front shows, and stays on screen.
- **Happened:** Panels hide while their app is not active, and Arbor never is: a panel that hides on deactivation would never show. An effect view that follows the app's state looks switched off. The test app's panels and dialogs need the same care.

No input was tried after the loss: the script's own tools cannot press by then. `check-F63.sh` passed 15 and failed 16, all for one reason that is still being probed: launched without the permission and then granted it by a write to the database, Arbor never heard yes (a-process-started-without-the-permission-goes-on-hearing-no), so its part that takes the permission away has still never run. The spec still says "the switch itself has not been tried".
- **Found by:** A census of the tests and specs, then the two scripts' first run.
- **Stand-ins play it:** partly (`FakeWindowSystem.isDenied`, `Harness.revokeAccessibility`, `FakeWindowSystem.flagLags`)
- **Guard:** `e2e: the permission goes` (by hand); `e2e: the permission returns` (by hand); `e2e: session 4: Accessibility is taken away while the taps are installed` (by hand)
- **Arbor copes:** **nobody knows**

## toolchain

Toolchain and machines: compilers, runners and shells that differ from the ones at hand.

### appkit-draws-an-images-handler-on-any-thread

*hurt 1 · below the seam · suspected · K923 · touches `crash`*

- **Expected:** A drawing closure written in a method of the main actor runs on the main actor.
- **Happened:** AppKit calls an image's drawing handler whenever and wherever it draws the image. Swift 6 traps a closure that inherited the main actor and is called elsewhere.
- **Found by:** Stated in six source files and in the backlog as a trap. No crash is on record.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** **none**
- **Arbor copes:** ArborArtwork and the panels' mask closures are `@Sendable` and use nothing but their arguments.
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/UI/ArborArtwork.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/UI/BackdropPanel.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/UI/FinderPanel.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/UI/HeadsUpPanel.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

### a-stream-configuration-does-not-keep-its-colour

*hurt 2 · below the seam · K829 · K842 · touches `crash`*

- **Expected:** A colour handed to a property of one of Apple's objects is kept by that object. Code that type-checked against stand-ins and was read would run.
- **Happened:** `SCStreamConfiguration.backgroundColor` does not retain its value. A colour made on the spot is gone by the time ScreenCaptureKit copies the configuration: the one time Arbor took pictures on a Mac it crashed in the first sweep, a second after launch, silently (SIGTRAP). That run's session at the real 0.46 s was lost with it, so the motion was filmed at 1.2 s only.
- **Found by:** The pictures' only run, in the motion's Mac shell script on a hosted Mac (macOS 26.6), where child processes have Screen Recording. The cure has been read, not run.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** `test: picturesOfWindowsAreOffUntilSomebodySaysOtherwise`
- **Arbor copes:** WindowPictures.noBackground is a static that outlives every configuration. The mended code has not run since, so pictures ship off (`windowPictures`).
- **Read in:** `Sources/ArborKit/UI/WindowPictures.swift`, `docs/features/F02-animated-transitions.md`, `docs/RELEASE-NOTES.md`, `collab/QUESTIONS.md`, `collab/parity.json`

### a-sockets-path-is-limited-to-103-bytes

*hurt 3 · machine · K133*

- **Expected:** The temporary folder, or any home folder, is a fine place for a socket.
- **Happened:** A socket's path is limited to 103 bytes on macOS (107 on Linux), and macOS's own temporary folder uses half of them. With a user name longer than about 50 characters `arborctl` cannot reach Arbor.
- **Found by:** Stated in the harness and in a review of the control socket. No run is named.
- **Stand-ins play it:** cannot: it lies below or beside the seam
- **Guard:** **none**
- **Arbor copes:** UnixSocket.address refuses a longer path with a message that gives both numbers; `ARBOR_SOCKET` is the way out, and the harness keeps its sessions under /tmp.
- **Read in:** `scripts/mac-shell/lib.sh`, `Sources/ArborIPC/UnixSocket.swift`, `Tests/ArborKitTests/ControlSocketTests.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`

*hurt 3 · machine · K1754*

- **Expected:** A fenced block with `# remarks` can be pasted whole into a terminal.

## What the stand-ins say they cannot imitate

In their own words, with the place where they say it. Nothing in this list is a reproach: a stand-in that names its limits is worth more than one that does not.

**The fake Mac (`Sources/arbor-fakemac`, `scripts/mac-shell/rehearse.sh`).** Files without a folder are in `Sources/arbor-fakemac`.

Whole subjects:

- It can say nothing about AppKit's and Accessibility's timing and order of notifications, animations, the finer points of which window is in front, the Dock growing and shrinking, Spaces and full screen, what anything looks like, or whether an event tap or a hot key really gets its events. "A rehearsal proves the script, not Arbor." (`main.swift`, `scripts/mac-shell/rehearse.sh`, `docs/TESTING.md`)
- Every picture of a rehearsal is one black pixel. (`scripts/mac-shell/rehearse/mac-tools`, `scripts/mac-shell/rehearse.sh`)
- It has one display. The tool that plugs in a virtual display has no stand-in, nor has the curtain. A script that plugs in a display, or compiles a tool of its own against AppKit, stops with exit code 2. (`main.swift`, `scripts/mac-shell/rehearse.sh`, `docs/TESTING.md`, `scripts/mac-shell/check-F49.sh`)
- It has no full screen: "nothing here could say anything true". (`World+TestApps.swift`)
- It has neither dark mode nor macOS's Spaces. (`collab/BACKLOG.md`, K1851)
- It has no app but the test windows: no TextEdit, Terminal or Calculator to open, and `open` launches nothing. (`scripts/mac-shell/check-F54.sh`, `scripts/mac-shell/check-F53.sh`, `World+Arbor.swift`)
- "There is nothing in this world that Arbor cannot see." (`Arbor.swift`)

Time:

- A whole second passes after every line that changes something, so debounced work (saving, putting windows back) has always happened by the next line. (`main.swift`, `World.swift`)
- A `sleep` of under a second does nothing; a longer one moves the fake clock and takes no time. (`scripts/mac-shell/rehearse.sh`, `World.swift`)
- How long the button is down, and how long a drag takes, are not modelled. An app that insists on its frame has done so, quick or slow, "by the time a quarter of a second is over". (`World+Pointer.swift`, `World+Pointer.swift`, `World+TestApps.swift`)
- Motion is recorded and not shown: the stage would be down again before anyone could look. (`Arbor.swift`)
- The date is a fixed day. (`World+Arbor.swift`)
- SIGKILL cannot be caught, so the stand-in for Arbor cannot say that it died; whoever comes next notices. (`Driver.swift`)

Copies that have to follow by hand:

- The decisions and log lines of the macOS-only code that scripts can see are repeated, each next to the name of what it repeats. When one of those changes, the fake Mac has to follow, and nothing says so. (`main.swift`, `World+Arbor.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`, K219)
- Of the system's facts it has "the little … that this Mac has an answer to". A rescue runs "with permission and without the alert". Where the app beeps at a refused URL, nothing happens. (`Arbor.swift`, `World+Arbor.swift`, `World+Arbor.swift`)
- No Mac's compiler has seen it: it is declared on Linux only. (`Package.swift`)

Windows and who is in front:

- The order of windows is the world's own: "the fake knows nothing of clicks and of apps coming forward". (`Arbor.swift`)
- The heads-up line and the panel of shortcuts are "recorded and not listed among the windows yet". (`Arbor.swift`)
- The wallpaper and the icons on it are left out of the list that decides what is under the pointer. (`World+Input.swift`)
- The furniture (menu bar, Dock, Finder's Desktop, Control Center's items) is what one hosted Mac listed before any session, stretched to the display; Arbor's menu bar item is where that Mac's menu bar put it. (`World+Pointer.swift`, `World+Menu.swift`)
- Sheets hang on windows only; only ordinary windows in front can be minimized, restored or given a tab; a tab that is not in front can be neither closed nor given the keyboard. (`World+TestApps.swift`)
- Guessed, not measured: that a window shrunk with `setContentSize` keeps its top left corner; how far swept windows move up or down; a panel's title bar of 22 points. (`World+TestApps.swift`, `World+Pointer.swift`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`, M678)

Input and the menu:

- The right button is modelled on Arbor's menu bar item only. Only Arbor's own shortcuts can be held down. An open menu takes every key, and "only Escape is modelled". (`World+Input.swift`, `World+Input.swift`, `World+Input.swift`)
- The keyboard layout is the US one, and hot keys are registered "in a world where no other app holds a shortcut". (`World+Arbor.swift`, `World+Arbor.swift`)
- In Go to… the real palette chooses when the button comes up; "nothing here tells the two apart". (`World+GoTo.swift`)
- The menu's sizes are made up; it has one level of submenus; About Arbor opens no panel and Open Settings File no editor. (`World+Menu.swift`)

The Mac's own commands:

- Only some of what a script uses is a stand-in. `rm`, `pkill`, `osascript`, `tccutil` and the rest would be the real ones, which is why a rehearsal refuses to run on a Mac. (`scripts/mac-shell/rehearse.sh`)
- Each stand-in knows the few uses that the scripts make of it and refuses the rest, with a message that names it and exit code 64. `lsappinfo` knows two forms. (`scripts/mac-shell/rehearse/mac-tools`, `main.swift`, `World.swift`)
- Its pointer tool and its test app are stricter than the real ones on purpose: they refuse what they do not know, where the real ones stay silent. (`World+Pointer.swift`, `World+TestApps.swift`)

Said nowhere, but so, by the code:

- Accessibility is always granted, and the tool's questions about permissions always answer yes. (`World+Arbor.swift`, `World+Pointer.swift`)
- A hand edit of settings.json is noted for later replays and never applied: there is no stand-in for the app's `SettingsWatcher`. (`World.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/App/SettingsWatcher.swift`)
- The peek's outline and the backdrop are not among Arbor's windows. (`collab/BACKLOG.md`, K1030)
- `killall` does nothing, so "restart WindowManager to make it read the setting" cannot be got wrong. (`scripts/mac-shell/rehearse/mac-tools`)
- A title bar is 32 points whatever the app, and a double-click on it and the green button both fill the screen or go back; the person's setting for the double-click is not asked. (`World.swift`, `World+Input.swift`)
- The fake pointer tool and the real one have drifted apart. The fake knows words the real one in the tree does not have, and refuses `activity`, `key --repeat` and `drag --no-settle`, which three scripts use. (`World+Pointer.swift`, `scripts/mac-shell/pointer.swift`)

**The fake window system and the chaos lab (`Sources/ArborTesting`)**

- A window still flying out of the Dock, or back from full screen, keeps its frame for 0 seconds by default: "not seen on a Mac so far", "but nobody has looked at a slow Mac or with ⇧ held". (`Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`)
- A plain change of displays leaves the windows at their old coordinates, "which no Mac does". (`Sources/ArborTesting/Chaos.swift`)
- After it learned to echo, the fake still leaves out repeated focus reports across apps, the Dock's two points at a minimize, and apps that settle late or on a grid. (`collab/BACKLOG.md`, K470)
- Of the sixteen rows of "What real macOS does that `FakeWindowSystem` does not", written at 07:00 UTC on 2026-10-14, eight are played at least in part today (echoes, focus answers, the reachable title bar, whole points, sizes, plain titles, focus before a restore and before a close). Not played: a drag that begins late, a press that focuses first, the second mouse-up, "resized" that stalls, unhiding that moves windows, a minimize that changes the display, an unresizable window's silence, and the time a `setFrame` takes. (`collab/evidence/traces/README.md`)
- `moveTogether` is implemented in the stand-in only. The real layer runs the protocol's default, which does nothing. (`Sources/ArborKit/Platform/WindowSystem.swift`)
- `strangers`, windows that Accessibility does not report, is set by no test, scenario or rehearsal. (`Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`)

**Traces, type-checks and pictures**

- What the real layer made of things is baked into a trace, so a fix below the seam does not change a replay. (`docs/TRACES.md`)
- No trace holds a double-click on a title bar, Safari, an Electron app, full screen, Spaces or a second display. All but one of the forty were recorded in one day on one hosted Mac with a single 1024×768 display. (`collab/evidence/traces/README.md`)
- `make typecheck-mac`: "A pass is not proof: a stand-in can be more lenient than the SDK, and nothing runs." Its page lists the known differences. (`scripts/typecheck-mac/README.md`, `scripts/typecheck-mac/README.md`)
- Pictures drawn off screen cannot show what the window server adds: blur, shadows, levels, which panel is in front, hover, clicks. (`docs/TESTING.md`)
- What the real-window runner says no headless test reaches: the order in which macOS reports a new window and its focus, whether Accessibility says that a window cannot be resized, what frame a window has at the moment it is reported, the app's own wiring of a switch and of settings.json, and whether the settings window opens, takes the keyboard and stays above Arbor's panels. (`Sources/arbor-e2e/NewWindows.swift`, `Sources/arbor-e2e/main.swift`, `Sources/arbor-e2e/main.swift`)

## Checks that exist and have never run on a Mac

As the repository's own documents say it. Three reasons recur. CI drives real windows with two things only, `scripts/e2e.sh --full-screen` and `scripts/mac-shell/e2e-drag.sh`; every other script is started by hand (`.github/workflows/ci.yml`). The Mac shell scripts were on hold from about 08:20 UTC on 2026-10-14, after a dangerous clean-up was found in one of them (`docs/RELEASE-NOTES.md`). And some scripts change the system so much that they end with exit code 77 on any Mac that is somebody's (`docs/TESTING.md`). "Rehearsal" is what the script did on Linux against the fake Mac at commit `a391fe4`, passed/failed; the column of that name in the backlog's table is from an earlier fake Mac and no longer holds.

**Rehearsals.** `rehearse.sh` has no list: it plays the scripts it is given, and whether one gets through is decided by what it touches. Every script played once at `a391fe4` (Swift 6.4 on Linux, bash 5.2, the default display): sixteen of fifty-one get through green, ten more reach their end with ✘, twenty-five stop or are cut off. Twelve stop because a tool of their own needs AppKit, three at a second display. `check-F12.sh`, which passed 40 of 40 on a Mac, rehearses 24/17, because the fake Mac applies no hand edit of settings.json. No gate runs a rehearsal: `make check` and CI do not call it, so the fake Mac drifts unnoticed (`Makefile`, K501).

Beside the table:

- **Steps that run and cannot fail.** The real-window runner only `observe`s what "nobody has seen on a Mac yet": a dialog over a window out of view is brought in, the palette has the keyboard by AppKit's and by Accessibility's word, it closes when the keyboard goes elsewhere, `reveal` of a hidden app's window, a window docked automatically has the keyboard, a native tab with automatic docking on. (`Sources/arbor-e2e/Misbehaving.swift`; `Sources/arbor-e2e/GoTo.swift`; `Sources/arbor-e2e/NewWindows.swift`)
- **CI presses no key.** arbor-e2e sends commands over the socket and posts no input; `e2e-drag.sh` uses the pointer only. So no shortcut, hot key, event tap, gesture or panel that takes the keyboard is exercised on a real Mac by CI. Both macOS jobs are left out when `scripts/ci-changes.py` decides that a Mac could prove nothing new. CI does not run `make check`, so not `scripts/test-tooling.py`, `scripts/privacy-smoke.sh` or `make rehearse`.
- **One run has pressed keys since.** A suite of real-window checks that is not on the trunk yet ran once on hosted Macs, on 2026-10-14 (its evidence is not in the repository yet, and none of the scripts named here is part of it). In it every shortcut that `arborctl bindings` lists was pressed with real key events and checked against the window server: 143 checks, all green. A peek was held and let go, green; the menu bar item was right-clicked and its items clicked. Its section with the ⌃⌥ rectangle, the ⌃⌥-click, the ⇧-drag and the ⌥-pinch has not run yet, nothing in it scrolls, and nothing in it switches Reduce Motion off. The table above is about each feature's own script.
- **Four scripts have left the table.** On 2026-10-15 `check-F51.sh` (35/0), `check-F63.sh` (15/16), `check-displays.sh` (110/19) and `input-taps.sh` (146/14; only a first version had run before) ran for the first time, one after the other on one hosted Mac, at `8aa9e10`, once, started by hand, with posted events. Peek, the ⌃⌥ rectangle, posted pinches and ⌃⌥ + scroll were green in every step; the taps were let go within a second of the permission's loss; a virtual second display can be made there. 13 of the 14 failures of `input-taps.sh` are the Desktop guard's, which is shelved. Their output is not in the repository. What is still unknown is under [never-exercised](#never-exercised).
- **Shipped off until seen on a Mac:** `windowPictures`, `guardDesktopClicks`, `holdStillWhileCameraIsOn`, `holdStillWhileMicrophoneIsOn`, `continuousZoom`, `tabsEnabled`, `minimapDuration` (0).
- **Never done by anybody:** a real lid closed, a real cable pulled, sleep and wake, mirroring, fast user switching, a logout with windows out of view, a pinch on a real trackpad, a real wheel, real keys pressed in any of the three panels that take the keyboard, the permission taken away by hand, a working day. (`docs/RELEASE-NOTES.md`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`)
- **"Compiled, and its picture tests pass on a Mac" is not "seen".** By the documents nobody has looked at the minimap, the name field, the palette, the backdrop and tiles, or the ring's flash on a screen.
- The backlog holds 266 questions "no script answers". Those on which a stand-in's model rests: which display stops a window whose corner is on none (M1366); how far down a window may go without a Dock, where the fake assumes 32 points (M665); whether Accessibility can move a window at all with no display connected (M1945); whether macOS moves windows back when a display returns (M1953); the order of `didActivateApplication` and `activeSpaceDidChange` (M1096); whether a background app's report is what `backgroundFocus` plays (M1968); whether a held shortcut repeats through Carbon hot keys, which `Harness` plays as "sends its press again and again" (M1082). (`collab/BACKLOG.md`)

## Evidence that is cited and is not in the repository

`collab/evidence/` holds `gestures-latest.txt` and `traces/`, and there is no `collab/reports/`. Cited all the same:

- **`collab/evidence/ax-events.txt`**, the recorded order of notifications on macOS 26 that `FakeWindowSystem.Echoes` says it is held to. Cited at `Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`, `Sources/ArborKit/Controller/Controller+Hold.swift`, in seven files under `Tests/ArborKitTests/` (FaithfulFakeTests.swift, HoldTests.swift, ParityProofTests.swift, ReviewLeadTests.swift, ReviewSwitchesTests.swift, ReviewTilingTests.swift, ReviewUndoTests.swift), `docs/TESTING.md` and two specs (`F30`, `F38`). `scripts/mac-shell/events.sh` with `axwatch.swift` records it anew on a hosted Mac.
- **`collab/reports/2026-10-14-review-ax.md`**, the measured facts about macOS numbered M1 to M23. Cited at `Sources/ArborKit/AX/AXWindowSystem.swift` and `Sources/arbor-e2e/Misbehaving.swift`. The probe that measured them is not under `scripts/mac-shell/` either (`collab/BACKLOG.md`, K517).
- **`collab/evidence/e2e-latest.txt`**, which `make parity` reads. CI uploads it as an artifact and nobody commits it, so every step of arbor-e2e counts as 0 and `docs/FEATURES.md` shows "real windows 0/n" for 24 items. (`docs/TESTING.md`, `scripts/e2e.sh`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, `collab/BACKLOG.md`, K518)
- **Other reports under `collab/reports/`**: the chaos lab's (`Tests/ArborKitTests/ChaosTests.swift`, `Tests/ArborKitTests/ChaosRegressionTests.swift`, `Tests/ArborCoreTests/RobustnessTests.swift`), one on appearance (`docs/features/F36-appearance-leftovers.md`), and five more named in `collab/QUESTIONS.md` and `collab/BACKLOG.md`. `CLAUDE.md` and `collab/README.md` still ask for a report there.
- **`collab/evidence/2026-10-14-F02-mac-shell.txt`**: `docs/features/F02-animated-transitions.md`, `docs/FEATURES.md`, `collab/parity.json`.
- **`collab/evidence/2026-10-14-review-ux-mac.txt`**, the run that showed all five WindowManager keys absent: `docs/features/F42-setup-check.md`.
- **`collab/evidence/screens/`**, among them the picture of the wallpaper click's sweep: `docs/features/F42-setup-check.md`, `docs/features/F60-guard-the-wallpaper-click.md`, `docs/KEYBOARD.md`, `docs/features/F58-hold-the-view.md`, `docs/features/F02-animated-transitions.md`.
- **`collab/evidence/focus-ring/`**: `docs/features/F37-focus-ring.md`. **`collab/evidence/compat-lab/`**: `Tests/ArborCoreTests/RealWindowDecisionTests.swift`. **`collab/evidence/state-files/`**: `docs/TESTING.md`, `scripts/fuzz-launch.py`. **`collab/evidence/keyboard.txt`**, still to be made: `scripts/mac-shell/probe-keyboard.sh`.
- **The one file that is there is old.** `collab/evidence/gestures-latest.txt` is one run of `proof.sh` on 2026-10-14 at 06:48 UTC: 101 passed, 8 failed. Its eight ✘ (restoring, switching apps, full screen) have been mended since and not run again. Its rectangle was drawn with ⇧⌘, which is no longer the default. It was recorded with macOS's edge tiling switched off (`collab/evidence/gestures-latest.txt`), which is why its green checks never met that second actor. (`collab/QUESTIONS.md`)

## The manners the stand-ins have today

Counted by grep at commit `a391fe4`. "Rude" means on unless a test switches it off; "polite" means that nothing happens unless a test asks. The last column gives `@Test` functions whose body names the knob / test files that name it anywhere, out of 5560 functions in 259 files; a knob set in a shared helper is undercounted in the first number. "lab" is the chaos lab (`Sources/ArborTesting/Chaos*.swift`), "sim" `Sources/arbor-sim`, "fake Mac" `Sources/arbor-fakemac`. FWS is `Sources/ArborTesting/FakeWindowSystem.swift`; other files without a folder are beside it.

| `echoes.focus` | FWS | rude | Arbor's `focus(_:)` comes back as one focus report after the call returns | every Harness test meets it; off only with `Echoes.none`, in 1 test |
| `echoes.frames` | FWS | rude | Arbor's `setFrame` comes back as one change nobody made by hand | as above |
| `echoes.keyboard` | FWS | rude | macOS moves the keyboard: to a new window, to the app's next window before a close or minimize is reported, to another app at ⌘H, to a window leaving the Dock | every test meets it; switched off in 13 / 8; the fake Mac toggles it per window |

| `FakeReleaseFeed.reply = nil`, `answer(_:keep:)` | FakeReleaseFeed.swift | polite | a slow network; a feed that answers twice | 4 / 1 and 3 / 1 |
| `MemoryTraceSink.failure` | Fakes.swift | polite | a full disk | 1 / 1 |
| `MemoryStateStore.repairs`, `keptCopy`, `loadProblem` | Fakes.swift | polite | a state.json that was damaged | 21 / 3; fake Mac |
| `World.isSwept` | Sources/arbor-fakemac/World.swift | rude, as the Mac's setting says | "Click wallpaper to reveal desktop": the window server has the windows at the sides, Accessibility where they were | rehearsals only; no `swift test` |
| `World.hungUntil` (`hang <seconds>`) | Sources/arbor-fakemac/World.swift | polite | a test app that does not answer for a time | rehearsals only |

Read as a whole:

- Five switches in `Echoes` are rude by default, all from one recording on macOS 26; since then macOS's tiling as well.
- Everything that imitates lateness (`focusIsSlow`, `defersFocus`, `restoresLate`, the two flights, `holdsEchoes`) is off by default and is switched on by 25 of 5560 tests. None of it is in arbor-sim, in the scenarios or in the fake Mac, and only `holdsEchoes` is in the chaos lab.
- No knob makes time pass while Arbor waits for an app, applies a call that timed out late, loses a destroy or a termination notice, moves other windows when one leaves full screen or an app is unhidden, nudges the Dock at a minimize, sends a focus report before "created", repeats a focus report, sends the half-way frame of a `setFrame`, lets a dragged window trail the pointer, stops a window at the menu bar, stops a raise short of the active app's key window, brings Finder forward when an app hides, delivers echoes app by app, or asks `WindowGrab` whether a drag is one.
- The chaos lab is polite too. Apps that fight back or hang appear only in the 30 % of runs that allow misbehaviour (`Sources/ArborTesting/ChaosGenerator.swift`). It never takes the permission away and never sets a size step, `stackingIsUnknown`, `flagLags` or `refusesTaps`. A failing script it does not know is only printed unless `ARBOR_CHAOS_STRICT=1`. Three of its rules are red by name today (`Sources/ArborTesting/ChaosKnownFailures.swift`).
- A new member of a seam that has a default implementation falls on that default behind the trace recorder, the replayer and the fake Mac until somebody forwards it, and nothing fails to compile. `TraceForwardingTests` is the net.
- **Once a stand-in has said the same as a Mac without being told.** Drags had been seen to go unnoticed on hosted Macs, and a run of the real-window suite had shown one with the pointer 27 points away at the first look. A model of a Mac under the real Accessibility layer (`make mac-on-linux`, on its way to the trunk), asked only how a drag can be lost, came to the same lines of the layer by its own road, on Linux, and said more: a drag of any length is lost for good once the pointer is far away at the first look (a-dragged-window-may-stand-still-until-the-pointer-is-24-points-away). The first run of `check-displays.sh`, made in the same hour by somebody who did not know of either, lost three of four long drags. Every other case on this page is a stand-in corrected by a Mac; here one agreed with a Mac beforehand. What share the script's coarse steps had in that run is for its trace to say.

## The hosted Macs

What the outputs of runs on 2026-10-14 show, label `macos-26` unless it says otherwise. `docs/TESTING.md` has the short form.

**The machine**

- macOS 26.6.2 on a virtual Apple M1: arm64, 3 cores, 7 GiB of memory, 95 GiB free. bash 3.2.57, Python 3.14.
- One display, 1024×768 points at scale 1. Visible frame (0,31 1024×674): the Dock takes 63 points. The display's identifier is the same on every Mac. The display can be switched to 1600×900 with a helper tool; there is no 1440×900.
- A script's own work begins six to seven minutes after the Mac started, with load averages above 30. Nobody has ever touched the Mac: the time since the last input equals the uptime. The pointer starts at (10,10), and no app has the keyboard.
- On the console, not locked, display awake, no screen saver. Display sleep and sleep are 0: these Macs do not sleep.
- Accessibility and Screen Recording are granted to the runner's child processes. An app bundle signed afresh and started through `open` is not trusted.
- Four event taps of system processes exist before Arbor starts, two of them enabled.
- Black wallpaper, light appearance, Finder in front.
- Every material of an effect view is drawn as one flat colour, (228,228,228) in light and (38,38,38) in dark, over any wallpaper. macOS's own menus and the Dock do tint. Blur and translucency cannot be judged there.
- A plain window's title bar is 28 points high.

**Defaults**

- `com.apple.WindowManager` holds none of `EnableTilingByEdgeDrag`, `EnableTopTilingByEdgeDrag`, `EnableTilingOptionAccelerator`, `EnableTiledWindowMargins`, `EnableStandardClickToShowDesktop`. So tiling at the edges, at the menu bar and with ⌥ is on, and a click on the wallpaper reveals the desktop. `doctor` reports all four as in the way.
- `AppleActionOnDoubleClick` is not set: a double-click on a title bar fills the screen.
- Reduce Motion is on, so Arbor shows no motion unless a script switches it off first.
- Displays have separate Spaces. VoiceOver is off. One input source, U.S.

**Swift**

- Xcode 26.0.1 to 26.6, that is Swift 6.2 to 6.3.3. No Swift 6.4 and no Xcode 27. The Mac's own compiler cannot build Arbor.
- Every job installs Swift 6.4.1 through swiftly (`scripts/ci-toolchain.sh`); the SDK stays Xcode's.

**The other images**, as a probe printed them. Nothing of Arbor's has run on them.

| Label | macOS | Machine | Swift selected | Display |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| macos-14 | 14.8.9 | virtual M1, 3 cores, 7 GiB | 5.10 | not printed |
| macos-15 | 15.7.9 | virtual M1, 3 cores, 7 GiB | 6.1.2 | not printed |
| macos-15-intel | 15.7.9 | x86_64, 4 cores, 14 GiB | 6.1.2 | 1920×1080 |

Jobs mostly started within ten seconds of being created. When more were wanted than Macs were given, five ran at a time and one waited eight and a half minutes.

**What real windows said on these Macs that day**

- At `51b162d` nothing was built: Swift 6.3.3.
- At `276f46c` arbor-e2e had 7 ✘ (three on new windows, two on the switch of apps, two of the small display) and `e2e-drag.sh` 7 passed, 11 failed.
- At `a391fe4` arbor-e2e had 4 ✘ in one run (two on the switch, two of the small display) and ended without a verdict in another (exit 6 after 31 s, unexplained); `e2e-drag.sh` passed 18 of 18 both times.
- The switch of apps was red in 6 of the 9 runs that reached it.
- Other scripts at `a391fe4`: `shots-F43.sh` 67 passed, 0 failed; `shots-F10.sh` 62/0 on one Mac and 61/1 on another; `shots-demo.sh` 18/2; `shots-F15.sh` 28/2; `shots-F12.sh` 59/12. Some of those failures nobody has read yet.
- A suite of real-window checks that is not on the trunk yet, in its first run: 1,406 of 1,454 passed. Six of the failures had been green in the rehearsal on Linux, each a stand-in politer than macOS: the raise, the menu that is cut off, ⌘H for an accessory app, drags, the heads-up line, macOS's own alerts.
- One script played six times on a hosted Mac and once in a rehearsal, and compared line by line: 319 differences, put down to 23 causes. 142 are the title bar's four points, 46 the number of echoes; one cause is a fault of Arbor's traces, one is only the rhythm of a drag, one (macOS's tiling) is worth a look at Arbor as well, and the rest are stand-ins politer than macOS. Each is a case above or has sharpened one.
- A day with nine real apps at macOS's defaults, 106 acts: no window lost, none left behind another in 72 switches, six faults (`collab/BOARD.md`).
- The same script at the same commit can give two answers on two Macs. In their first minutes these Macs are busy.
